14: # Theming a chart from DESIGN.md
15: 
16: Open this when a chart has to wear a measured site's look, or when a themed delivery's palette, corners and provenance have to be checked against the reference it came from.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Purpose
23: 
24: Apply one locally available v3 `DESIGN.md` to a copy of an existing chart form, with the palette gates and a provenance record intact.
25: 
26: ### When to Use
27: 
28: - A request names a local `DESIGN.md`, a measured site's look or another v3 Style Reference.
29: - A `design-md` delivery's provenance, palette or corners have to be checked.
30: - A `--default` delivery has to be reproduced or explained.
31: 
32: ### Boundaries
33: 
34: `DESIGN.md` is a style reference, not a chart form. The chart packet applies one locally available
35: v3 reference to a copy of an existing form; it does not extract a site, open a URL or change the
36: stock palette. Extraction belongs to `sk-design-md-generator`.
37: 
38: ---
39: 
40: ## 2. THE COMMAND
41: 
42: The `DESIGN.md` input must be a local file. A URL is refused. The output directory is created only after every chosen form has a complete derived palette and both theme validations have passed. There is no force option.
43: 
44: ```bash
45: node .skilled/skills/sk-design/sk-design-chart/scripts/apply-design-md.cjs \
46:   path/to/DESIGN.md --forms grouped-bars,daily-line --out scratch/themed
47: ```
48: 
49: - Use `--all` instead of `--forms` to copy every form.
50: - `--scheme light|dark|both` selects which ground receives the reference: `light` derives the light ground and keeps the stock dark chrome, `dark` derives the dark ground and keeps the stock light chrome, and `both` derives both when the reference declares dark support. If a reference is light-only, its dark half is the stock dark chrome with series re-derived against it.
51: - `--tokens tokens.json` supplies the optional sibling token inventory explicitly; otherwise a sibling `tokens.json` is used when present.
52: 
53: An ordered form (`bullet`, `calendar-grid`, `heat-matrix`, `progress-single`) paints a single-hue
54: magnitude ramp with step and end gates of its own. A colour table does not supply such a ramp, so
55: the script never themes an ordered form: naming one is refused, and `--all` skips it with a note.
56: Those forms keep the stock ordered system inside an otherwise themed set.
57: 
58: ---
59: 
60: ## 3. WHAT THE PARSER READS
61: 
62: The parser follows the v3 headings rather than searching for arbitrary prose:
63: 
64: | Reference section | Required shape | Used for |
65: | --- | --- | --- |
66: | `## Tokens — Colors` | `Name`, `Value`, `Token`, `Role` table | Chrome roles, chromatic series and emphasis |
67: | `## Tokens — Typography` | First typeface heading and its immediate `Substitute` line | Body stack, and mono heading when the reference supplies one |
68: | `## Tokens — Spacing & Shapes` → `### Border Radius` | `Element`, `Value` table | The five chart corner rungs |
69: 
70: A missing heading, table or substitute is reported by name and stops the run. Six-digit colour
71: values are the usable rows; gradients are not silently turned into flat colours.
72: 
73: ---
74: 
75: ## 4. THE ROLE MAPPING
76: 
77: The mapping preserves the chart packet's role vocabulary and uses table order as prominence:
78: 
79: | Chart role | Selection |
80: | --- | --- |
81: | `surface` | The lightest colour whose role names a background, surface, canvas, ground, panel or fill |
82: | `ink` | The darkest text-role colour on the light ground, and the lightest text-role colour on the dark ground |
83: | `muted` | A text-role colour nearest the stock muted ratio that still clears the text gate |
84: | `rule` | The selected ink colour held at the stock dark-rule alpha |
85: | `series-1` through `series-4` | Chromatic table values that clear the mark gate, each taken verbatim, chosen greedily by hue distance from the hues already chosen so no two neighbours share a hue; a pair that is both under the separation ratio and within thirty degrees of hue is refused as one colour. When fewer than four clear, the table's own neutral text tones fill the remaining series darkest first, with the ink held back until last so it stays free for emphasis. No value is adjusted |
86: | `emphasis` | The most saturated remaining chromatic value that clears the mark gate and the emphasis floor against series 1; when every clearing hue is spent on series, the ink, as the stock categorical system does |
87: 
88: The lightest and darkest background/text choices are calculated separately for each ground. A
89: declared dark `DESIGN.md` theme, or a supported `darkMode` in `tokens.json`, supplies the dark
90: ground. Otherwise the stock dark surface, ink, muted value and alpha rule stay in place and only
91: the series are re-derived against that ground. No colour is borrowed from the three stock semantic
92: systems to fill a missing chromatic role.
93: 
94: The corner ladder uses the largest measured radius that does not exceed each stock rung. A rung
95: with no measured value below its ceiling keeps the corpus value; it never grows a corner beyond the stock
96: ladder. The measured primary typeface precedes its substitute stack in every body declaration, and every declaration that already names a monospace face takes the reference's mono stack; the choice is by what the declaration is, not by where it sits. A
97: dedicated mono typeface is used when the reference supplies one; otherwise the primary stack is
98: used for the mono declarations as well.
99: 
100: A table colour counts as chromatic when its HSL saturation is at least 24 percent; below that it
101: is a neutral and can only serve the chrome roles or fill a missing series. The threshold keeps a
102: warm grey out of the series ladder while letting a muted brand hue in.
103: 
104: ---
105: 
106: ## 5. THE DEFAULT REFERENCE
107: 
108: When a request names no Style Reference, `--default` themes from
109: `assets/style-reference/evilcharts/DESIGN.md`, the one reference this packet carries beside its
110: forms and the one the stock palette source is derived from since v0.18.0.0. It applies that
111: reference's own table to the shared roles as one derived system, so the delivery and the stock
112: palette agree where the mapping lands on the same value and differ where it has to choose one,
113: which is the larger part of the colour table. The corner ladder is what reproduces the stock
114: values exactly, all five rungs byte-identical, and that is the property that says the default is
115: still the reference the corpus came from. The check holds the palette file against that reference
116: through the `palette-derivation` family; a themed delivery is held against the gates instead.
117: 
118: The copy is severed from its source on purpose. A reference that is regenerated elsewhere would
119: change what `--default` produces without a diff, and leave the stock palette derived from a file
120: that no longer exists. `assets/style-reference/evilcharts/origin.md` records where the copy came from
121: and pins each file by hash. Overriding is unchanged: pass any other `DESIGN.md` path, including one
122: `sk-design-md-generator` has just produced, and the script themes from that instead.
123: 
124: ---
125: 
126: ## 6. THE CORNER LADDER IS A FLOOR, NOT A MAPPING
127: 
128: Each of the corpus's five rungs takes the largest corner the reference publishes that still fits it.
129: A reference with nothing that small has said nothing about that rung and the corpus value stands,
130: the way an ordered form keeps the stock ramp when a colour table cannot supply one. It used to
131: collapse to zero instead, which squared every data mark, legend swatch and progress capsule in a
132: themed set and said nothing about having done so.
133: 
134: The stock reference publishes 4.4, 6.4, 8.4 and 12.4px. Under the floor its 4.4 lands on track,
135: swatch and pill and its 8.4 on the card, which is the stock ladder exactly; the 2px mark corner is
136: below anything it publishes, so the corpus value stands. What the floor costs is worth stating rather
137: than leaving to be discovered: a reference whose corners are all larger than the corpus rungs
138: contributes none of them.
139: 
140: Mapping by the reference's own element names instead — its `cards` row straight to the card rung —
141: was measured and rejected. It happens to agree with the floor for this reference, whose `cards` row
142: is 8.4px, and it disagreed for the one before it, which named a 4px card and would have handed the
143: rung a corner the stock ladder had deliberately not taken. The floor is the rule that reproduced the

18: ---
19:

21: 
22: ### Purpose
23: 
24: Apply one locally available v3 `DESIGN.md` to a copy of an existing chart form, with the palette gates and a provenance record intact.
25: 
26: ### When to Use
27: 
28: - A request names a local `DESIGN.md`, a measured site's look or another v3 Style Reference.
29: - A `design-md` delivery's provenance, palette or corners have to be checked.
30: - A `--default` delivery has to be reproduced or explained.
31: 
32: ### Boundaries
33: 
34: `DESIGN.md` is a style reference, not a chart form. The chart packet applies one locally available
35: v3 reference to a copy of an existing form; it does not extract a site, open a URL or change the
36: stock palette. Extraction belongs to `sk-design-md-generator`.
37: 
38: ---
39: 
40: ## 2. THE COMMAND
41: 
42: The `DESIGN.md` input must be a local file. A URL is refused. The output directory is created only after every chosen form has a complete derived palette and both theme validations have passed. There is no force option.
43: 
44: ```bash
45: node .skilled/skills/sk-design/sk-design-chart/scripts/apply-design-md.cjs \
46:   path/to/DESIGN.md --forms grouped-bars,daily-line --out scratch/themed
47: ```
48: 
49: - Use `--all` instead of `--forms` to copy every form.
50: - `--scheme light|dark|both` selects which ground receives the reference: `light` derives the light ground and keeps the stock dark chrome, `dark` derives the dark ground and keeps the stock light chrome, and `both` derives both when the reference declares dark support. If a reference is light-only, its dark half is the stock dark chrome with series re-derived against it.
51: - `--tokens tokens.json` supplies the optional sibling token inventory explicitly; otherwise a sibling `tokens.json` is used when present.
52: 
53: An ordered form (`bullet`, `calendar-grid`, `heat-matrix`, `progress-single`) paints a single-hue
54: magnitude ramp with step and end gates of its own. A colour table does not supply such a ramp, so
55: the script never themes an ordered form: naming one is refused, and `--all` skips it with a note.
56: Those forms keep the stock ordered system inside an otherwise themed set.
57: 
58: ---
59: 
60: ## 3. WHAT THE PARSER READS
61: 
62: The parser follows the v3 headings rather than searching for arbitrary prose:
63: 
64: | Reference section | Required shape | Used for |
65: | --- | --- | --- |
66: | `## Tokens — Colors` | `Name`, `Value`, `Token`, `Role` table | Chrome roles, chromatic series and emphasis |
67: | `## Tokens — Typography` | First typeface heading and its immediate `Substitute` line | Body stack, and mono heading when the reference supplies one |
68: | `## Tokens — Spacing & Shapes` → `### Border Radius` | `Element`, `Value` table | The five chart corner rungs |
69: 
70: A missing heading, table or substitute is reported by name and stops the run. Six-digit colour
71: values are the usable rows; gradients are not silently turned into flat colours.
72: 
73: ---
74: 
75: ## 4. THE ROLE MAPPING
76: 
77: The mapping preserves the chart packet's role vocabulary and uses table order as prominence:
78: 
79: | Chart role | Selection |
80: | --- | --- |
81: | `surface` | The lightest colour whose role names a background, surface, canvas, ground, panel or fill |
82: | `ink` | The darkest text-role colour on the light ground, and the lightest text-role colour on the dark ground |
83: | `muted` | A text-role colour nearest the stock muted ratio that still clears the text gate |
84: | `rule` | The selected ink colour held at the stock dark-rule alpha |
85: | `series-1` through `series-4` | Chromatic table values that clear the mark gate, each taken verbatim, chosen greedily by hue distance from the hues already chosen so no two neighbours share a hue; a pair that is both under the separation ratio and within thirty degrees of hue is refused as one colour. When fewer than four clear, the table's own neutral text tones fill the remaining series darkest first, with the ink held back until last so it stays free for emphasis. No value is adjusted |
86: | `emphasis` | The most saturated remaining chromatic value that clears the mark gate and the emphasis floor against series 1; when every clearing hue is spent on series, the ink, as the stock categorical system does |
87: 
88: The lightest and darkest background/text choices are calculated separately for each ground. A
89: declared dark `DESIGN.md` theme, or a supported `darkMode` in `tokens.json`, supplies the dark
90: ground. Otherwise the stock dark surface, ink, muted value and alpha rule stay in place and only
91: the series are re-derived against that ground. No colour is borrowed from the three stock semantic
92: systems to fill a missing chromatic role.
93: 
94: The corner ladder uses the largest measured radius that does not exceed each stock rung. A rung
95: with no measured value below its ceiling keeps the corpus value; it never grows a corner beyond the stock
96: ladder. The measured primary typeface precedes its substitute stack in every body declaration, and every declaration that already names a monospace face takes the reference's mono stack; the choice is by what the declaration is, not by where it sits. A
97: dedicated mono typeface is used when the reference supplies one; otherwise the primary stack is
98: used for the mono declarations as well.
99: 
100: A table colour counts as chromatic when its HSL saturation is at least 24 percent; below that it
101: is a neutral and can only serve the chrome roles or fill a missing series. The threshold keeps a
102: warm grey out of the series ladder while letting a muted brand hue in.
103: 
104: ---
105: 
106: ## 5. THE DEFAULT REFERENCE
107: 
108: When a request names no Style Reference, `--default` themes from
109: `assets/style-reference/evilcharts/DESIGN.md`, the one reference this packet carries beside its

111: reference's own table to the shared roles as one derived system, so the delivery and the stock

# sk-design-chart References

The reference set answers four questions in order: which chart form answers the comparison the reader needs, what colour means in the chart, how a local `DESIGN.md` becomes a delivery and what the file has to contain.

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

Four files sit here, each one a lookup or a contract rather than a guide to read end to end. Load the one the table names for the question in front of you.

| Load | When |
| --- | --- |
| [`catalog.md`](./catalog.md) | **First, always.** Maps a comparison to one chart form and the file that draws it |
| [`color-system.md`](./color-system.md) | Before choosing a palette, and whenever a request asks for more categories than a system carries |
| [`design-md-theming.md`](./design-md-theming.md) | When applying a local v3 `DESIGN.md` or reviewing a provenance-gated delivery |
| [`template-contract.md`](./template-contract.md) | Before authoring or editing any template file |

The catalog holds twenty-nine chart forms across six question families. When no row answers the question in front of you, defer with the gap named rather than answering freehand, because a freehand chart is what the template-first rule exists to prevent.

---

## 2. WHAT BELONGS HERE

Reference files in this packet are lookups and contracts. They route a request to a template and they carry no render code of their own, because a render block copied into a reference is a second copy that drifts from the template it came from.

Chart markup lives in `../assets/`. Stock colour values live in `../assets/style-reference/evilcharts/palettes.json` and nowhere else. A local design reference is read by `../scripts/apply-design-md.cjs`, and this directory holds the guide that defines how its values earn the same roles and gates.

---

## 3. WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT

**Report mode.** There is no report catalog and no multi-chart report page, and none is planned. A report is a second product with its own layouts, its own selection rules and its own index, and nothing in the chart capability depends on it. The capability analysis this packet was built from recommended leaving it out and that recommendation was taken.

**Galleries.** There are no gallery pages. One chart form is one file, the catalog points straight at it, and a new form starts as a copy of a whole skeleton file rather than as a block extracted from a page of demos. The reason is the one `template-contract.md` gives: what reaches a reader is a delivery, and a gallery ships every other form's demo data alongside the one they asked for.

13: ---
14: 
15: # Chart Colour Systems
16: 
17: Colour belongs to the Style Reference it was measured from. Every reference under
18: `assets/style-reference/` carries its own `palettes.json` beside its `DESIGN.md`, and the corpus
19: check fails a reference that carries none, so adding a reference is deciding its colour rather than
20: inheriting whichever palette happens to be the default.
21: 
22: What a reference owns is its colour, not the floors that colour has to clear. The contrast gates,
23: the type scale and the corner ladder are read from the default reference's file and apply to every
24: delivery, whichever reference painted it — a brand supplies values, it does not get to lower the bar
25: those values are measured against. A second reference's own `palettes.json` records the measurement
26: behind its values and is not read while that reference is not the default, which is why adding one is
27: a decision about colour and not about accessibility.
28: 
29: Every stock colour in this packet comes from the default reference's file,
30: `assets/style-reference/evilcharts/palettes.json`. A template never invents one, and the corpus
31: check fails a template that carries a colour literal anywhere except a palette block. A `design-md` delivery is the one request-time exception: its values come from a local v3
32: `DESIGN.md`, and the checker accepts them only by provenance plus the same inline gates.
33: 
34: Every role holds two values, one per ground. A file paints the light set by default and the dark set when the reader's operating system asks for one, and both sets come from the same file and clear the same gates.
35: 
36: ---
37: 
38: ## 1. OVERVIEW
39: 
40: ### Purpose
41: 
42: Three built-in systems exist. A fourth identifier, `design-md`, is a request-time adapter for a
43: local v3 Style Reference rather than a fourth semantic encoding. Pick one built-in system per
44: stock delivery, or use the adapter with its provenance and gates.
45: 
46: ### When to Use
47: 
48: - Before a delivery picks its palette, and whenever a request asks for more categories than a system carries.
49: - When a row's `system` cell has to be settled against the definitions in section 2.
50: - When applying a local v3 `DESIGN.md` or reviewing a provenance-gated delivery.
51: 
52: ---
53: 
54: ## 2. THE QUESTION EACH SYSTEM ANSWERS
55: 
56: A colour system is an answer to "what does colour mean in this chart". That is the axis that
57: separates the three built-in systems. `design-md` answers a different question: which measured
58: local style reference should fill the same role vocabulary while the data encoding remains the
59: form's existing one.
60: 
61: | System | `encodes` | Colour encodes | Use it when | Capacity |
62: | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
63: | `neutral` | `importance` | Rank, by lightness alone. The series run from the value furthest from the ground: darkest first on paper, brightest first on ink | The default, and the fallback whenever hue would carry no stable meaning | 4 series |
64: | `ordered` | `magnitude` | Position on a scale | The data is ordered: a value, a rank, a time position, a progress figure | 5 steps |
65: | `categorical` | `category` | Category membership | The categories are unordered and there are four or fewer | 4 categories |
66: | `design-md` | `reference` | A measured local style mapped into the chart roles; the data still follows the form's declared encoding | The request names a v3 `DESIGN.md`, style reference or measured site's look | 4 series |
67: 
68: Start at `neutral`. Reach for another only when the data has the property that system encodes. A categorical palette on ordered data throws away the ordering, and an ordered ramp on unordered categories invents one. `design-md` is selected by the presence of the local reference, not by a new data meaning.
69: 
70: ### Two names for one system
71: 
72: The second column exists because two vocabularies name these three built-in systems and both are
73: load-bearing. The id is what a file declares in its meta tag and what a catalog row carries. The
74: `encodes` value is a separate field in the palette source, and the contrast gates in section 5 and
75: the enforced list in section 6 are written against it rather than against the id, because what a
76: gate holds depends on what the colour means and not on what the system is called. They map one to
77: one, in the order above. A failure message quotes whichever of the two the rule it came from reads,
78: so the mapping is written here rather than inferred from a message.
79: 
80: `neutral` used to be described in this table as encoding nothing, which contradicted both the
81: palette source and the rest of its own row. Lightness is colour, and ranking by it is what
82: `importance` names.
83: 
84: ### What the shadcn comparison kept
85: 
86: The shadcn comparison measured a much tighter categorical light-theme set than the standalone
87: one: shadcn light has a 16.0° minimum adjacent hue gap and 1.72:1 minimum own/opposite-ground
88: contrast, while standalone categorical light has a 92.9° gap and 3.37:1 minimum own/opposite-ground
89: contrast. The dark measurements were 71.1° and 2.92:1/2.15:1 for shadcn, against 96.5° and
90: 3.38:1/1.72:1 for standalone categorical. The numbers support keeping the standalone role split
91: and its existing gates rather than replacing it with a raw five-token ramp; they do not create a
92: new CVD or hue threshold here.
93: [SOURCE: specs/sk-design/018-sk-design-parent-v2/001-sk-create-chart/013-shadcn-reference-research/research/lineages/luna/research.md:55-66]
94:

421: ### The card reads as a product, not a template
422: 
423: Five rules from the polish pass, each held by the checker.
424: 
425: - **The source line is the source.** The visible `data-chart-part="source"` text names where the
426:   numbers came from and nothing else; the instruction that retargeting means replacing the data
427:   block lives in a comment directly above `CHART_DATA`. The `source-line` family errors when that
428:   instruction creeps back into the line a reader sees.
429: - **The plot is the largest thing on the card.** Cartesian forms draw in a 392-unit-high frame on
430:   the 720-unit width, about 54 percent, with the baseline, tick row and legend moved down with the
431:   frame. Forms whose shape does not fill a taller frame (calendar grid, heat matrix, unit grid and
432:   ring, treemap, progress, bullet, funnel, independent percentages, population pyramid) keep their
433:   own height.
434: - **The table folds, it never leaves.** The data table sits inside `<details class="data">` with a
435:   "Show the data" summary, open on every form, and keeps `data-chart-table` on the table itself
436:   so the accessibility and card-readout checks read it unchanged. It used to start closed wherever
437:   a tooltip answered the pointer, which left the tooltip as the only visible source of the values,
438:   one hover per number. The `table-disclosure` family holds the wrapper, the summary and the open
439:   state.
440: - **A finding declares its direction.** A `FINDING` block beside `READOUT` carries `trend` as
441:   `up`, `down` or `none` with a one-line reason; the footer draws a 12px inline arrow in the
442:   emphasis colour for up or down and nothing for none. A share, a comparison or a spread is
443:   `none`; only a change over time earns an arrow. The `finding-cue` family holds the block, the
444:   set and the read.
445: - **Numbers carry their unit and ticks stay short.** `READOUT.unit` is a short string, or empty
446:   when the card mixes units, printed after the value with a thin space; every tooltip form
447:   declares it. Axis ticks at or above five digits render through a hand-written `compact()` as
448:   `12k` or `1.2M` with one decimal at most, while the card and the table keep full digits, and
449:   `toLocaleString` and `Intl` stay forbidden.
450: 
451: ### A card may lead with its number
452: 
453: A form whose data has an honest baseline declares a `METRIC` block beside `READOUT` and prints a
454: value, a signed delta and the period above the plot. `present` is `true` or `false` in every form,
455: so the decision is written down rather than implied: nineteen forms declare `false` because a
456: share, a distribution or a matrix has no earlier reading to compare against, and the block's own
457: `why` line says so.
458: 
459: - **The value is a literal.** `value` and `valueLabel` name a number the reader can find in the
460:   table; the delta is computed from the same data and never at draw time. A form that would have to
461:   invent either declares `present: false`.
462: - **The rung is published.** The value prints at the `metric` rung, 26px, which lives in the palette
463:   source beside the other roles, so the type-scale family accepts it without a template-local size.
464: - **The delta carries the same cue as the finding.** Up or down draws the 12px arrow, coloured by
465:   the emphasis role for a fall and the second series role for a rise, then the delta phrase and the
466:   period in muted text.
467: - **`present: false` means no element.** The `metric-block` family errors when a form declares the
468:   block absent and still ships the markup, and when a form ships the markup with no block at all.

471: 
472: The light block carries one more kind of shared value: the five corner rungs, `--chart-radius-mark`
473: through `--chart-radius-card`. They are not colours and they live in their own object in the
474: palette source, but they are emitted into the same block because every file already carries that
475: block and the check already compares it against the source in both directions. They appear once
476: and only in that block, since a corner is the same corner on either ground. The rungs are the
477: measured ladder: 2px for a mark, 4.4px for a track, a swatch and the pill, 8.4px for the card
478: that holds the chart.
479: 
480: A corner is never typed into a file. A stylesheet reaches a rung the way it reaches a colour, and
481: SVG marks take theirs from CSS too: `rx` is a geometry property, so `.box { rx: var(--chart-radius-mark); }`

427:   block lives in a comment directly above `CHART_DATA`. The `source-line` family errors when that
428:   instruction creeps back into the line a reader sees.

430:   the 720-unit width, about 54 percent, with the baseline, tick row and legend moved down with the
431:   frame. Forms whose shape does not fill a taller frame (calendar grid, heat matrix, unit grid and
432:   ring, treemap, progress, bullet, funnel, independent percentages, population pyramid) keep their
433:   own height.

435:   "Show the data" summary, open on every form, and keeps `data-chart-table` on the table itself
436:   so the accessibility and card-readout checks read it unchanged. It used to start closed wherever
437:   a tooltip answered the pointer, which left the tooltip as the only visible source of the values,
438:   one hover per number. The `table-disclosure` family holds the wrapper, the summary and the open
439:   state.

441:   `up`, `down` or `none` with a one-line reason; the footer draws a 12px inline arrow in the

15: # Chart Template Contract
16: 
17: A template is one HTML file. It opens on a double click, with no install, no package manager and no build step, and it keeps working when the person who received it edits the numbers by hand.
18: 
19: ---
20: 
21: ## 1. OVERVIEW
22: 
23: ### Purpose
24: 
25: State the contract one chart template file meets: the card parts, the data and readout blocks, the dependencies it may not take and the twenty-five rules the corpus check enforces.
26: 
27: ### When to Use
28: 
29: - Before authoring a template, or before editing one that already ships.
30: - When a corpus check failure names a rule and the reader needs the contract behind it.
31: - When deciding whether a dependency, a computed value or a pointer affordance is allowed.
32: 
33: ### Core Principle
34: 
35: Both of those properties are load-bearing. The reader is a writer or an operations analyst rather than a developer, and the file has to survive being emailed to somebody who will open it on a laptop with no network.
36: 
37: ---
38: 
39: ## 2. THE DELIVERY UNIT
40: 
41: One file holds one chart. Inside it, the visible unit is a card with five parts in a fixed order.
42: 
43: | Part | Marker | What goes in it |
44: | --- | --- | --- |
45: | Headline | `data-chart-part="headline"` | A conclusion, not a chart type. "Revenue by plan" is a label. "Where we gained and where we bled" is an argument |
46: | Subtitle | `data-chart-part="subtitle"` | The legend and the time range, in a sentence |
47: | Figure | `data-chart-part="figure"` | The drawing itself |
48: | Footer | `data-chart-part="footer"` | The one-line finding in ink, separated from the figure by the rule |
49: | Source | `data-chart-part="source"` | The muted description line in the footer; where the numbers came from |
50: 
51: - The fixed five are what make a chart legible with no caption around it.
52: - The headline rule is the highest-value writing rule in this packet: a reader who takes nothing but the top line should still have learned something.
53: - The footer is part of the card rather than a caption added around it: the finding tells the reader what to notice, and the source stays attached to that reading.
54: 
55: ### Gallery and delivery are different things
56: 
57: A delivery is one card in one file, and it is what reaches a user. A gallery is many cards on one page, used as a workbench for finding a form. Never hand over a gallery. It carries every other chart's demo data with the user's one real chart somewhere inside it.
58: 
59: ---
60:

## 3. HOW IT WORKS

The workflow is template-first, and that is a constraint rather than a preference. A chart assembled from a form file renders the way that file already rendered. A chart written freehand does not, and the failure shows up in a browser rather than in a check.

When the request names a `DESIGN.md`, a style reference or a measured site's look, route the
application branch to `scripts/apply-design-md.cjs`. It reads the v3 headings documented by
`references/design-md-theming.md`, derives both grounds from local values, and writes themed
copies only after the corpus gates pass. A request that asks for themed charts without naming a
reference runs it with `--default`, the evilcharts reference carried at `assets/style-reference/evilcharts/`. If the request asks to create the Style Reference itself,
route that extraction to `sk-design-md-generator`; this packet owns application, not extraction.

1. Read the request and name the comparison the reader needs to make.
2. Open `references/catalog.md` and resolve that comparison to one row.
3. Copy the file that row names. Do not rewrite its render code.
4. Swap the data block for the reader's data.
5. Apply one colour system from the default reference's palette. One per artifact.
6. Keep the result a single self-contained file. It opens in a browser with no install step.
7. Run the corpus check before reporting the result: `node scripts/check-corpus.cjs` over the packet, and `node scripts/check-corpus.cjs --extra <dir>` over a delivery written outside it. Both must print `RESULT: PASSED`.

## 3. HOW IT WORKS

The workflow is template-first, and that is a constraint rather than a preference. A chart assembled from a form file renders the way that file already rendered. A chart written freehand does not, and the failure shows up in a browser rather than in a check.

When the request names a `DESIGN.md`, a style reference or a measured site's look, route the
application branch to `scripts/apply-design-md.cjs`. It reads the v3 headings documented by
`references/design-md-theming.md`, derives both grounds from local values, and writes themed
copies only after the corpus gates pass. A request that asks for themed charts without naming a
reference runs it with `--default`, the evilcharts reference carried at `assets/style-reference/evilcharts/`. If the request asks to create the Style Reference itself,
route that extraction to `sk-design-md-generator`; this packet owns application, not extraction.

1. Read the request and name the comparison the reader needs to make.
2. Open `references/catalog.md` and resolve that comparison to one row.
3. Copy the file that row names. Do not rewrite its render code.
4. Swap the data block for the reader's data.
5. Apply one colour system from the default reference's palette. One per artifact.
6. Keep the result a single self-contained file. It opens in a browser with no install step.
7. Run the corpus check before reporting the result: `node scripts/check-corpus.cjs` over the packet, and `node scripts/check-corpus.cjs --extra <dir>` over a delivery written outside it. Both must print `RESULT: PASSED`.
